sources.title: MIVUBI Performance Watchdog and Scheduler Budget Policy v1

facts.subject: scheduled work
facts.statement: Classify scheduled work as CRITICAL_NOW, SOON, BACKGROUND, or RECOVERY. Only critical-now work may consume the immediate tick path without batching; lower-priority work must be deferred, distributed, or coalesced.

facts.subject: multi-arena work budget
facts.statement: Each arena generation gets a bounded scheduler budget for scans, retries, world verification, entity setup, and recovery so simultaneous arenas cannot each consume an unbounded full-tick workload.

facts.subject: global script budget
facts.statement: Per-arena budgets must also obey a global runtime budget; local compliance is insufficient if many arenas or recovery jobs run concurrently.

facts.subject: entity/world scanning
facts.statement: Do not perform unfiltered full-world entity scans or equivalent wide queries on a per-tick hot path when narrower filters, registries, spatial bounds, or event-driven updates can satisfy the requirement.

facts.subject: polling and retry
facts.statement: Polling/retry loops must define maximum attempts, minimum interval, exponential or staged backoff where appropriate, and a terminal state. Many independent one-tick retries are prohibited when the condition is slow-changing.

facts.subject: duplicate scheduled work
facts.statement: Requests for the same logical verification/recovery target within a generation should coalesce behind one in-flight operation instead of spawning duplicate intervals, jobs, or scans.

facts.subject: runJob generator design
facts.statement: runJob generators must yield at fine-grained, bounded units of work and avoid iterations whose single step can itself perform an unbounded scan or large mutation batch.

facts.subject: repeating callbacks
facts.statement: Repeating work that can outlive its nominal interval must have an in-flight/ownership guard so a new iteration cannot start while the prior generation's operation is still active.

facts.subject: worldLoad recovery
facts.statement: worldLoad/restart reconciliation must phase and queue expensive recovery work instead of starting every arena scan, lease repair, entity reconciliation, and structure verification in the same tick window.

facts.subject: stable runtime lookups
facts.statement: Cache stable handles/metadata that do not need per-tick recomputation, while still revalidating handles whose lifecycle can become invalid. Avoid repeated dimension/config/constant lookup work inside hot loops.

facts.subject: performance evidence
facts.statement: Treat profiler data and measured call counts as the primary evidence for hot-path optimization. Static suspicion may trigger investigation, but optimization claims should be tied to measured runtime evidence where possible.

facts.subject: watchdog terminate event
facts.statement: Do not rely on cancelling or handling watchdog termination as the main resilience strategy. Prevent budget violations and maintain crash-safe recovery because termination cancellation may be unavailable or unsafe.
